```{r setup, include = FALSE}
# Root locator + dual-load idiom shared with the get-started vignette: the
# source tree (check and site-build contexts) loads through pkgload; a bare
# installed package (reader-side) loads through library().
.pkg_root <- function() {
  for (dd in c(".", "..", "../..")) {
    if (file.exists(file.path(dd, "DESCRIPTION")) &&
        file.exists(file.path(dd, "R", "treatment-report.R"))) return(normalizePath(dd))
  }
  NA_character_
}
PKG <- .pkg_root()
if (!is.na(PKG) && requireNamespace("pkgload", quietly = TRUE)) {
  suppressWarnings(suppressMessages(pkgload::load_all(PKG, quiet = TRUE,
                                                      export_all = TRUE)))
} else {
  library(msuiter)
}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

`ms_compare()` is the calibrated-similarity face of the package: it matches
two signature sets under a chosen protocol, scores each match with a
similarity metric, and attaches **null distributions** so a cosine is
never read without its sampling context. This guide covers the comparison
container, the exposure-level group test, and the clustering/embedding
post-fitting analyses.

## Two sets of signatures

A synthetic cohort generated under two exposure programs, extracted de
novo, and compared against the generating reference — the everyday
"did we recover the processes?" question:

```{r cohort}
ref <- ms_refdb_bundled()$SBS_GRCh38@matrices[[1]]
S   <- ref[, c(1, 5, 9)]
colnames(S) <- paste0("CS", 1:3)
E1  <- matrix(rep(c(0.5, 0.3, 0.2), each = 12), 3, 12)
E2  <- matrix(rep(c(0.2, 0.5, 0.3), each = 12), 3, 12)
E   <- cbind(E1, E2)
sim <- ms_simulate(S, exposures = E, burden = 3000, seed = 3)
ext <- suppressWarnings(ms_extract(sim, k = 3))
```

## The comparison container

`ms_compare()` takes the estimated and reference signature matrices (the
channel rows must match), the two exposure matrices for the activity
protocol, and the null-distribution controls. The result is an
`MsComparison` — a metrics table keyed by signature pair, with raw and
BH-adjusted null probabilities:

```{r compare}
cmp <- ms_compare(ext@signatures, S,
                  exposures_est = ext@exposures, exposures_ref = E,
                  null_n = 200, null_n_draws = 500, seed = 1L)
cmp
```

The metrics table carries the cosine per matched pair plus the `p_null`
and `q_bh` columns; the protocol field names the match protocol family
applied. `metric` selects the similarity measure (cosine by default), and
`protocol` switches between the Hungarian assignment, the Islam greedy
threshold sweep, and the Jiang activity protocol. Two practical notes:
the Jiang activity face is only defined when **both exposure matrices**
are supplied, and the default run evaluates the full protocol family —
so a signatures-only comparison (no exposures) must restrict the
protocol, e.g. to the Hungarian assignment:

```{r protocol}
cmp_isl <- ms_compare(ext@signatures, S, protocol = "islam",
                      exposures_est = ext@exposures, exposures_ref = E,
                      null_n = 200, null_n_draws = 500, seed = 1L)
cmp_isl
```

The null faces: an analytic null (catalog-shape conditioned) and an
empirical Monte-Carlo null controlled by `null_n`, `null_n_draws`, and the
`seed` (the seed is gated to the same bounded range as every other FFI
face). Comparing two *extracted* sets — not one against a reference — uses
the same call with the second matrix in the `reference` position.

## Group differences in exposure

```{r minimal-compare}
cmp_min <- ms_compare(ext@signatures, S, protocol = "hungarian",
                      null_n = 200, null_n_draws = 500, seed = 1L)
cmp_min
```


`ms_exposure_test()` asks a per-signature question: does this signature's
activity differ between two sample groups? It returns a tidy table with a
raw and a BH-adjusted Wilcoxon-style test per signature:

```{r exposure-test}
grp <- factor(rep(c("early", "late"), each = 12))
et  <- ms_exposure_test(ext@exposures, grp)
et
```

A signature with `pass_bh = TRUE` under a real design is a candidate
etiological or temporal difference — the test is diagnostic, and its
assumptions belong to the exposure scale you pass in.

## Clustering and embedding

Two post-fitting analyses round out the comparison family.
`ms_cluster_signatures()` groups signatures whose pairwise similarity
exceeds a threshold (connected components over the threshold graph) and
names a medoid per cluster:

```{r cluster}
cl <- ms_cluster_signatures(ext@signatures, threshold = 0.9)
cl
```

`ms_embed()` projects the sample × signature exposure matrix into a
low-dimensional space (k-means by default; UMAP when the suggested
package is installed):

```{r embed}
em <- ms_embed(ext@exposures, method = "kmeans", clusters = 2, seed = 1)
head(em)
```

Both results have dedicated figure types — `plot_similarity_heatmap()`,
`plot_exposure_heatmap()`, and `plot_embedding()` — shown in
[the visualization gallery](visualization-gallery.html).
